newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh to pursue non-inflationary growth.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh to pursue non-inflationary growth.

text.p: Bangladesh Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria said on Saturday his government would pursue strictly a growth strategy that did not fuel inflation.
"We will stick to our non-inflationary growth strategy. We like to assure the consumers that our economic policies will not raise the price level," Kibria told reporters.
Kibria is expected to announce the national budget for fiscal 1997/98 (July-June) in parliament on June 12.
"So far we have been successfully containing the inflation rate, and we will sustain the effort. Growth with inflation does never benefit people," the minister said.
Kibria said the twelve-monthly average inflation rate was now slightly below four percent against 4.07 percent in July 1996.
The minister earlier held pre-budget consultations with different professional groups and said he was planning to meet with opposition political parties.
"We are trying to get a feeling about the expectation of people before the budget. The government wants to be maximum accountable and transparent."
The minister said he was expecting GDP growth to exceed 5.5 percent, targeted for the current 1996/97 fiscal year ending June 30.
He indicated he was basically banking his optimism on a good rice crop.
Kibria said major sectors of the economy were also performing well.

The minister said revenue collection, although lagging about two billion taka ($45 million) behind the target during the last ten months to April'97, would touch the projected mark by end of the financial year.
The minister referred to the level of foreign currency reserves, currently $1.8 billion, and said: "We need to add another 400 to 500 millions."
Bangladesh is negotiating with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) for a soft loan assistance between $500 and $600 million, officials said.
The minister told a questioner that the banking sector was now in the "most stable situation" in last 20 years.
"It is now better supervised than anytime before. Laws are being strengthened to effectively deal with bad-loan crisis."
According to the central bank, banks in Bangladesh were grappling with 135 billion taka ($3.08 billion) in defaulted loans.

Bangladesh's central bank governor Lutfar Rahman Sarkar triggered alarm last month by saying that country's banking sector was on the verge of collapse due to huge accumulation of non-performing loan.
Sarkar later said he had been misquoted.
